extracted.intended_audience: applicants and recipients of NIH grants (PD/PIs, institutional grants administrators, grants management officials)
extracted.subtask_description: Official NIH terms, conditions, and requirements for multiple PD/PI applications and for construction, modernization, or major alteration and renovation (A&R) of research facilities, covering application, review, budgeting, procurement, design, and post-award administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: eRA Commons registration required
rubrics_metrics.description: All PD/PIs must have established eRA Commons accounts with a PI role prior to application submission. When multiple PD/PIs are at different organizations, all organizations must also be registered in the eRA Commons. If the contact PD/PI is at a different institution from the applicant organization, then the applicant organization must also affiliate the contact PD/PI with their institution. Beyond the contact PD/PI, it is not necessary for all other PD/PIs to be affiliated with the applicant organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure account(s) and organizational registrations are in place before submission; affiliate contact PD/PI with applicant organization if contact is at a different institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leadership Plan required for multiple PD/PIs
rubrics_metrics.description: All multiple PD/PI applications are required to include a Leadership Plan whose purpose is to facilitate and enhance scientific productivity and establish a decision-making process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Plan must: describe a rationale for choosing the multiple PD/PI approach; describe governance and organizational structure of leadership team and research project (including communication plans, decision-making processes, procedures for resolving conflicts); delineate roles and administrative, technical, and scientific responsibilities for the PD/PIs, including responsibilities for human subjects or vertebrate animal studies as appropriate. Applicants may include budget allocation information for specific PD/PIs as part of the Leadership Plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: New investigator / early stage investigator classification rules
rubrics_metrics.description: An application will be considered a new investigator application only when all of the PD/PIs meet the NIH definition of new investigator, and similarly for early stage investigator status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serving as a PD/PI on a substantial independent PD/PI research award counts as serving as a PD/PI for purposes of losing new/ESI status. However, being added as a PD/PI to an active substantial independent award does not remove new investigator status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-project application PD/PI vs subproject lead distinction
rubrics_metrics.description: Lead investigators of subprojects/components of multi-project applications (e.g., P01, P30) are not automatically PD/PIs of the entire program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a subproject lead is also a PD/PI of the entire program, that individual must be specifically designated as a PD/PI on the application; do not confuse subproject leads with program PD/PIs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budgets for multiple PD/PI applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally, multiple PD/PI applications will submit a single budget for the entire project (applies to both modular and detailed budgets). The $250,000 modular threshold is for the entire project, not per PD/PI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When PD/PIs are at different institutions, follow standard consortium budget instructions. Applicants may include budget allocation information in the Leadership Plan; requested allocations may be reflected in a term in the Notice of Award (NoA) if awarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal or resubmission changes in PD/PI makeup
rubrics_metrics.description: A renewal or resubmission application may change from single to multiple PD/PIs or change the number/makeup of PD/PIs, but the applicant must provide a rationale and include the required Leadership Plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similarly, a previous multiple PD/PI application may change to single PD/PI in renewal/resubmission with a rationale provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competing revision PD/PI requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A competing revision to an existing multiple PD/PI grant must be submitted using the same Contact PD/PI as the parent grant and may propose changes in the Leadership Plan or composition of leadership with a rationale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A competitive revision to a single PD/PI grant may propose multiple PD/PIs provided a Leadership Plan is included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review of multiple PD/PI applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The review criteria applied to multiple PD/PI applications are the same as single PD/PI applications; each application is evaluated on its own merit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer reviewers will consider each PD/PI's qualifications and identified role. The leadership approach and quality of the Leadership Plan will be used to assess understanding of scientific complexities and project management and will be considered as part of the overall approach and scientific/technical merit. Reviewers will not recommend removal of individual PD/PIs but may recommend deletion of specific aims/budgets for a PD/PI, effectively removing that effort. SRG must evaluate the application in its entirety without dropping components.

rubrics_metrics.name: PD/PI listing and reporting responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: All PD/PIs are listed on the Summary Statement, NoA, and NIH databases. Responsibility for required reports is shared by the PD/PIs and the recipient institution; only one of each required report should be submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although all PD/PIs are responsible for report content, only one PD/PI should upload information in eRA Commons; only the recipient Signing Official may submit reports to NIH (including closeout reports).

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-award award administration for multiple PD/PI awards
rubrics_metrics.description: If multiple PD/PIs are from multiple organizations, NIH will issue the award to the applicant organization which administers the award using consortium or subaward arrangements. Budgets (including indirect costs on subawards) are determined per existing policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipient organization remains responsible for securing and retaining required written assurance signatures from each identified PD/PI for post-submission information, progress reports, and prior approval requests (including adding/dropping a PI).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior approval and changes in PD/PI status
rubrics_metrics.description: All existing prior approval requirements apply to multiple PD/PI awards (including change in status or addition of a PD/PI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a PD/PI withdraws or is no longer able to work on the project, submit a revised Leadership Plan or description of impact (e.g., change to single PD/PI) as part of the prior approval request; NIH will evaluate requests considering project as a whole including scope and budget impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact PD/PI affiliation and transfer considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Contact PD/PI changes institutions, the recipient institution must consider options because the Contact PD/PI must be affiliated with the recipient institution in the Commons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Options include designating another PD/PI as the Contact or relinquishing the grant for transfer. Contact PD/PIs considering transfer should consult the NIH awarding IC early.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions: Construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Construction: construction of a new building, structure or facility, including installation of fixed equipment, which provides space not presently available. Excludes purchase of land and ancillary improvements (parking lots, roads, fencing). Construction of shell space is not allowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shell space not considered construction because it does not provide usable space for research activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions: Modernization
rubrics_metrics.description: Modernization: alteration, renovation, remodeling, improvement, expansion or repair of, or completion of shell space in an existing building necessary to make the building suitable for program purposes; distinct from construction in that the existing structure remains in place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When primary purpose of award is modernization, the grant cannot support the conduct of any research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alteration & Renovation (A&R) and major/minor determination
rubrics_metrics.description: A&R activities are considered modernization and may be supported under research grants where primary purpose is other than construction/modernization. The NIH Program Official determines whether A&R is major or minor; Major A&R is unallowable under foreign grants and foreign components in domestic grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minor A&R projects are not required to satisfy all chapter requirements; major A&R projects are subject to this chapter’s requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory authority required for construction/modernization awards
rubrics_metrics.description: An IC must have specific statutory authority to issue awards with the primary purpose of construction or modernization. Even with authority, recipients may not incur costs unless NIH specifically authorizes such costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH generally issues construction/modernization awards under grants/cooperative agreements specifically for that purpose; recipients retain primary responsibility for project but NIH staff may be substantially involved under cooperative agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for construction/modernization grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Only public or private non-profit entities located in the United States or U.S. territories/possessions are eligible to apply for construction or modernization grants. For-profit and foreign organizations are not eligible. Major A&R is unallowable under foreign grants and foreign components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must confirm institutional eligibility before applying.

rubrics_metrics.name: NOFO and program-specific requirements for construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Construction grant applicants are required to apply in response to a specific Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO); RFAs are generally used; PAs may be used for ongoing programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any program-specific requirements will be included in or referenced in the NOFO and NoA; consult NOFO and program guidelines when applying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application review and award characteristics for construction/major A&R
rubrics_metrics.description: Construction, modernization, and major A&R applications are subject to peer review; specific review criteria are included in the NOFO. Construction/modernization grants usually involve a single award for the entire project and incremental funding is normally not used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AOR must sign the NoA to indicate acceptance of terms and return it to the GMO; funding may be limited by appropriations law (31 U.S.C. §1552(a)); consult GMO if activity unlikely to be completed within project period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title to site requirement and legal opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH expects that the applicant holds (or will hold) fee simple title or another estate/interest (e.g., leasehold) in the site where construction/modernization/A&R will be performed; NIH will determine compliance during administrative review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application must include a legal opinion describing the applicant's interest in the performance site, mortgages or foreclosable liens (principal, interest rate, dates, terms), appraised value, and any provisions protecting Federal interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matching requirement for construction grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise specified by statute, the rate of Federal financial participation in a construction project cannot be more than 50 percent of allowable construction costs. NIH can waive this requirement but only upon request prior to application submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Matching may be in the form of allowable costs incurred by the recipient or contractor. Third party in-kind contributions are generally not allowed as matching except on exception basis approved by the GMO and must meet 2 CFR Part 200.306 documentation and allowability requirements. Source and amount of matching funds must be identified and demonstrated available for the award duration; exceptions to 'cash on hand' require negotiation with NIH and may take the form of an assurance. Downward adjustments after award are a prior approval action; failing to obtain NIH approval may be a terms violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to ensure funds for operation after construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipient must ensure availability of sufficient funds for operation or continued operation of the facility after construction/modernization is completed to allow effective use of the facility for grant-supported purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should demonstrate operational funding plans in their proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procurement requirements for construction services
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipient procurement must comply with 2 CFR Parts 200.317–200.327 and must use contracting methods that ensure all qualified contractors have opportunity to bid/propose and that contracts will result in completion of a facility ready for occupancy, conforming to approved design/specifications, at a cost within the owner's ability to pay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless authorized by NIH, all NIH grant-supported construction/modernization/major A&R work must be procured by formal advertising resulting in lump-sum, fixed-price contracts using Design-Bid-Build. NIH may authorize other methods when sealed bidding is impractical. Recipient must obtain NIH approval of final construction documents before solicitation and before award; ensure project completion per approved plans or secure NIH approval for material changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accurate cost estimating and use of bid alternates
rubrics_metrics.description: Accurate cost estimating and the use of bid alternates (additive or deductive) are basic means to ensure contract award near the budgeted amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a precise description of scope, specifications, materials, and techniques to facilitate accurate estimates. Additive alternates may incorporate necessary features so long as they do not expand the scope of the peer-reviewed and approved project; selected alternates may be used in determining the low aggregate bid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Options if bids exceed available funds
rubrics_metrics.description: If all bids exceed funds despite deductive alternates, the recipient may (1) decline to award and, after NIH approval, issue a revised invitation for bids with changes; (2) negotiate with the low bidder (with NIH approval for design/spec changes); (3) negotiate with the next lowest bidder if low bidder refuses; or (4) cancel and rebid if negotiations fail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All design and specification changes from negotiations must be approved by NIH.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bidding for NIH-paid portion of larger project
rubrics_metrics.description: If NIH-supported project is less than entire facility, recipient must obtain bids/proposals that provide costs for the portion paid by NIH and required matching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This may be accomplished by dividing the project by building/site with separate costs or, if indivisible, by identifying or prorating applicable costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liquidated damages provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Invitations for bids must stipulate a time for completion (calendar days or fixed date) for each prime contract; at recipient option, a liquidated damages provision may be included to assess damages when contractor fails to complete by the date specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Liquidated damages must be realistic, justified, and approved by NIH before solicitation. Amounts paid belong to the recipient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design-Bid-Build project delivery requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The traditional Design-Bid-Build is the default three-phase project delivery: design phase, construction bid phase (solicitation and selection of contractor), then active construction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the prescribed procurement model unless NIH authorizes alternates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate contracting methods authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of contracting methods other than Design-Bid-Build (e.g., construction management, design-build) may be authorized by NIH when cost, time, and quality benefits will result; NIH will consider scope, estimated cost, and other factors and must approve before recipient begins process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain NIH approval before pursuing alternate contracting methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction Manager (CM) as Agent procurement
rubrics_metrics.description: Construction management services for technical consultation and oversight may be procured on a negotiated basis (professional services) or by formal advertising if prohibited by state/local law; bidders should be pre-qualified when invited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CM (as Agent) responsibilities include cost estimates, cost control, design review for value engineering, consultation on techniques, coordination, scheduling, and oversight. CM fee is an eligible cost for total eligible project cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction Manager-at-Risk (CM-at-Risk) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A CM-at-Risk assumes financial risk for construction at a Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP), serves as general contractor, and provides consultation during design and construction; terms must preclude conflicts of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CM must provide 100% performance and payment bonds; GMP must be obtained from the CM before NIH authorizes the first construction contract; each separately contracted portion must be separately priced in the GMP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design-Build procurement and selection requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Design-build is a single-contract delivery where firms submit designs meeting performance requirements within a GMP. Selection must allow maximum feasible competition and may include departures from formal advertising (cost treated as competitive factor, award regardless of number of proposals, negotiations permitted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection process must include preparation of an RFP describing design/cost/qualification standards and criteria, public announcement, consideration of qualified proposals, and selection of the firm judged best considering qualifications and RFP criteria. Recipient must ensure contract provisions that make extra costs from errors/omissions the design-build firm's responsibility and justify cost comparability with similar construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: GMP method may be used with CM-at-Risk or design-build; project must be completed at or below GMP. GMP must be itemized by trade separating labor, materials, markups, and only contingency for approved change orders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipient must transmit all GMP bids to the GMO with award recommendation. After GMP approval, GMP subcontracts must be competed with at least three bidders. Required steps: issue 'sources sought' announcement, pre-qualify firms, establish bidders lists, solicit by written invitation, consider any qualified contractor who requests to bid. If three bids cannot be obtained, submit a written explanation to GMO with supporting documentation. Unexpended funds due to lower costs must be refunded/credited to recipient and then to NIH. All subcontract prices must be approved by GMO; awards made to lowest-priced responsible, responsive bidders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design documentation and funds release conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Following award acceptance for construction/modernization grants or funds for major A&R, the design phase may begin but funds for construction/modernization or major A&R will not be released until final architectural drawings, specifications, construction schedule, and updated cost estimates are reviewed and approved by the NIH IC (unless NoA indicates otherwise).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advertisement for bids may only be initiated after final construction documents are approved by the NIH awarding IC. Procurement methods (including plans with CM/GMP) must be reviewed and approved by the awarding IC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum design requirements and codes/standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Working drawings and specifications submitted for NIH approval must conform to minimum standards in 42 CFR Part 52b.12 and the NIH Design Requirements Manual; recipients are subject to standards in effect at time of design/construction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must ensure project meets applicable State and local codes; if using State/local codes in lieu of NIH requirements, NIH awarding IC must determine equivalence or that State/local codes exceed NIH requirements. If State/local requirements are more stringent, the more stringent apply. Consider extended usage requirement (e.g., 10 or 20 years) when planning/designing.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH monitoring of design compliance and consultation
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH will monitor compliance with design requirements during design and construction phases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants/recipients with questions about applicability of Design Requirements Manual should consult the NIH Program Official (PO).

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal opportunity and labor standards inclusion in contract documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Labor standards and equal employment opportunity (EEO) requirements for federally assisted construction must be specified in bidder information and included in resulting contract documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include provisions required by 2 CFR Part 200, Appendix II to Part 200 in contract documents. Note: NIH construction/modernization grants and major A&R projects are not subject to Davis-Bacon Act unless the authorizing statute specifically requires compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal Employment Opportunity regulatory requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracts (and subcontracts) for construction (including modernization or major A&R) are subject to 41 CFR Part 60-1 as implemented by the OFCCP (U.S. Department of Labor).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the Department of Labor/OFCCP for additional information and compliance guidance (e.g., http://www.dol.gov/ofccp/).

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract Work Hours and Safety Standards applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Contractors and subcontractors providing construction services under NIH construction/modernization grants or major A&R projects with contracts or subcontracts exceeding $100,000 are subject to the Contract Work Hours and Safety Standards Act (40 U.S.C. 3701 et seq.) regarding payment of overtime and maintaining healthful and safe working conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure contracts include provisions to comply with overtime pay and safety standards for covered contracts.
